audit_findings.title: Affiliate earnings may be double-counted with the separately added stakes
audit_findings.magnitude: $138m, $85m and $105m of filed affiliate income in 2025, 2024 and 2023; $1.728bn of stakes added in the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate income would increase historical OE and its trend while the associated equity-method investments are also added through the stakes bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Turkey segment represents Seaboard’s non-controlling 52.5% investment in Butterball, which is accounted for using the equity method.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that consolidated earnings contain affiliate income, including Butterball and other affiliates. The record does not establish whether the OE calculations removed it. If retained, 2025 affiliate income alone equals 87.3% of the $158.1m anchor, so the overlap is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce a year-by-year OE reconciliation identifying and removing income from Butterball, STF, Daily’s, CT&M and all other affiliates, then recompute the anchor and all scenarios while leaving the stakes bridge unchanged.

audit_findings.title: Investment gains may be double-counted with cash and short-term investments
audit_findings.magnitude: $39m, $19m and $85m of filed net investment gains in 2025, 2024 and 2023; $1.207bn of cash and short-term investments added in the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Realized and unrealized portfolio gains would increase OE and the fitted anchor while the underlying portfolio is separately added at current value.
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in the fair value of short-term investments are recorded as unrealized gains and losses included in other income, net in the consolidated statements of comprehensive income, with any purchases and sales recorded on a settlement date basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that investment gains entered reported earnings, but the methodology states only that portfolio interest income was purged. It does not establish removal of gains. The positive gains equal 24.7% of the anchor in 2025 and 53.8% in 2023, making the possible double count material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile other income for every OE year, remove interest, dividends and all realized and unrealized gains or losses attributable to separately added investments, and rerun the trend and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The OE trend may retain large, reversing tax-valuation adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: $212m filed charge in 2024 and $170m filed benefit in 2025, equal to 134.1% and 107.5% of the $158.1m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The charge would depress 2024 OE, while its reversal would inflate 2025 OE; both observations influence the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Seaboard recognized $170 million of income tax benefit during 2025 as a result of changes in the valuation allowance in the U.S.
audit_findings.explanation: The adjustments are demonstrated, but their retention in OE is unresolved. Their opposite directions do not make them harmless because the log trend is sensitive to the timing and level of each annual observation. Each adjustment exceeds the anchor and can materially alter normalized OE.
audit_findings.action: Trace the tax line in the 2024 and 2025 OE schedules, strip both valuation-allowance entries symmetrically, substitute normalized cash taxes, and recompute the full OE series and anchor.

audit_findings.title: Unmonetized production tax credits may have been treated as current owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $66m recognized in 2025 inventory and cost of sales; $55m of net proceeds received upon sale of 2025 credits in the second quarter of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Accrual recognition can increase OE before cash realization unless the corresponding inventory build is deducted through working capital; embedding the credits in terminal OE could also overstate durable growth.
audit_findings.evidence: These credits are able to be monetized upon a sale to a third party, and there were no production tax credit sales for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $66m accrual is demonstrated, while its treatment in the OE calculation is unresolved. The amount is 41.7% of the anchor. The subsequent $55m realization supports substantial economic value but also demonstrates an $11m discount and a timing difference; it does not establish that 2025 OE or terminal OE handled the item correctly.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $66m income recognition, the related 2025 inventory increase and the $55m subsequent proceeds; rerun OE with consistent cash realization and separately exclude unsupported post-program credits from terminal earnings.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal could escape OE after amortization is added back
audit_findings.magnitude: $40m of filed 2025 finance-lease ROU amortization and $38m of filed 2025 finance-lease principal payments
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease amortization without deducting principal or equivalent replacement capital would increase OE despite the recurring cash payment for the leased assets.
audit_findings.evidence: Finance lease cost is recognized based on the effective interest method for the lease liability and straight-line amortization of the ROU asset.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed amounts demonstrate a potential near-dollar-for-dollar mismatch, but the OE treatment is not supplied. The $38m principal payment equals 24.0% of the anchor, so omission is reasonably capable of changing intrinsic value and the margin-of-safety conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify finance-lease ROU amortization within each D&A add-back, confirm whether finance-lease principal or equivalent replacement capital was deducted, and rerun OE for any unmatched amount.

audit_findings.title: EDM IV creates a discrete take-or-pay exposure outside historical OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $315m filed estimated EDM IV project cost; $344m of total filed capital commitments, primarily EDM IV, with the EDM IV take-or-pay amount not separately quantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Required construction spending and fuel purchases during a commissioning delay could reduce future OE or require an equity-value reserve that is absent from a smooth historical-OE forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: If the project is not completed on time, Seaboard has a take-or-pay fuel purchase contract that begins in 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking exposure rather than a demonstrated error in historical OE. The project cost equals 6.1% of the $5.156bn base equity value, but the filing does not isolate the take-or-pay amount or establish that a delay will occur. It should therefore be monitored and scenario-tested rather than treated as a present loss.
audit_findings.action: Track milestone spending, completion timing and commissioning status; obtain the EDM IV-specific annual minimum fuel quantities and prices, then run an explicit delayed-start scenario including remaining capex and take-or-pay payments without revenue.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $8.0m computed 2022 residual, equal to 3.4% of filed 2022 D&A and 5.1% of the $158.1m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Leaving potentially eligible D&A as an expense lowers 2022 OE and may modestly lower the fitted anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $227.0m (96.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative. Even assuming, more favorably than the record supports, that the entire $8.0m were recurring anchor OE, proportional application to the $2.221bn base operating value would add about $112m, or 2.2% of the $5.156bn base equity value and about $117 per share. The corresponding buy-below increase would be about $82 per share to roughly $3,850, still below the $4,323.58 market price; therefore it would not change the margin-of-safety conclusion.
audit_findings.action: No immediate rerun is required. Classify the residual from filed depreciation schedules and rerun 2022 and the trend only if evidence establishes that some portion is an eligible non-economic add-back.
